facts.text: Director Héctor Olivera co-produced the 1982 Argentine original, Last Days of the Victim, then came back to direct this English-language remake for Roger Corman.
Director Héctor Olivera's company Aries met Roger Corman through producer Alejandro Sessa at the Manila Film Festival. That meeting led to the Corman-Aries partnership that eventually made ten films.
This was one of ten movies cult producer Roger Corman made in Argentina in the 1980s, and it was shot in Buenos Aires with an Argentine crew and cast.
Why Argentina? Roger Corman got skilled technicians at bargain rates thanks to a favorable dollar-to-peso exchange rate, and Olivera's Aries was the only Argentine company that owned its own studios.
The story comes from José Pablo Feinmann's novel Last Days of the Victim. For this version, Feinmann rewrote it with US screenwriter Yolande Turner for a North American audience.
Corman's first Argentine hit, Deathstalker (1983), was publicized as a $2.5 million movie. It actually cost about $500,000, a common bit of budget inflation in Corman's publicity.
Star Don Stroud was once the world's 4th-ranked surfer. He also played his own drums in The Buddy Holly Story (1978).
The story began as Últimos días de la víctima, the first novel by Argentine author José Pablo Feinmann, published in Buenos Aires in 1979 and filed under 'novela negra', Spanish for noir fiction.
Don Stroud (James Conrad) survived a plane crash on Von Richthofen and Brown (1971) by treading water for 45 minutes and keeping the pilot alive.
Feinmann's hitman novel got three screen versions: the 1982 Argentine film, this 1989 Corman remake, and a 1995 French-Cuban TV movie, Les derniers jours de la victime, directed by Bruno Gantillon.
Adrianne Sachs (Cecilia Lorca) was Miss Brazil 1986. She also appeared in RoboCop (1987) and was on the covers of more than 500 romance novels.
The 1982 original, directed by Adolfo Aristarain, was Argentina's submission for the Best Foreign Language Film Oscar at the 55th Academy Awards. It was not nominated.
Don Stroud posed as the nude centerfold of Playgirl's November 1973 issue and was paid $10,000.
Federico Luppi played the hitman in the 1982 original. He also starred in Olivera's other Corman picture Cocaine Wars (1985), as Gonzalo Reyes opposite John Schneider's DEA agent.
Variety called Two to Tango 'uneven' when it came out. It also played under the Spanish title Matar es morir un poco, meaning 'To Kill Is To Die a Little'.
Duilio Marzio (Paulino Velasco) won a fellowship to Lee Strasberg's Actors Studio in New York in 1960 and stayed two years. He had left a law firm job to go on stage.
Duilio Marzio (Paulino Velasco) won an ACE Award in 1998 for playing writer Jorge Luis Borges in the play Borges y Perón. He later acted opposite Faye Dunaway in Jennifer's Shadow (2004).
The original Last Days of the Victim ranked 23rd in a 2000 survey of the 100 greatest Argentine films. This Corman remake is far less revered.
Olivera's Barbarian Queen (1985) was part of a nine-picture Aries-Corman deal to cash in on Conan the Barbarian. Star Lana Clarkson did all her own stunts.
Héctor Olivera won a Silver Berlin Bear for Rebellion in Patagonia (1974). He also made Funny Dirty Little War (1983), then directed Corman's Barbarian Queen and this film.
Michael Cavanaugh (Dean Boyle) played George Fox in 22 episodes of the sci-fi series Starman (1986-87). He also appeared in Star Trek: The Next Generation and The X-Files.
Michael Cavanaugh (Dean Boyle) later played Judge Austin Gorg in Holes (2003) and a forensic dentist in Red Dragon (2002), and has appeared in more than 100 films.
Film historian Tamara Falicov wrote that Olivera and producer Alejandro Sessa approached Corman around 1982, about when Argentina returned to democracy, to make low-budget films there.
Adolfo Aristarain, who directed the 1982 original, later made A Place in the World (1992). Its Oscar nomination was disqualified because Uruguay, his wife's country, had submitted it instead.
Don Stroud was stabbed ten times, including in his right eye, while helping a mugging victim in Greenwich Village in the early 1990s. He can no longer see out of that eye.
Alberto Segado (Lorenzo 'Lucky' Lara) trained at the University of Buenos Aires' Instituto de Teatro and spent much of his career at the Teatro General San Martín. He died in 2010 aged 66.
This was the final film for Maria Fournery, who plays Airline Attendant 2.
Olivera stepped in to direct Cocaine Wars after Corman clashed with the imported director. The film was nearly titled The Bolivian Connection, to echo The French Connection.
The soundtrack uses tango music by Argentine bandleader Raúl Garello and his orchestra, including 'Che Buenos Aires' and 'Margarita de Agosto'.
Corman's first Aries hit, Deathstalker, grossed about $11.9 million in the US on a roughly $500,000 budget, though sources indicate it was never released in Argentina.
